nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable spaces, $P$ a measure on $X$ and $Q$ a measure on $Y$. A coupling of $P$ and $Q$ is a probability measure $\pi$ on $X \times Y$ whose marginals are $P$ and $Q$: the pushforward of $\pi$ under the projection $X \times Y \to X$ is $P$, and its pushforward under the projection $X \times Y \to Y$ is $Q$. The set of couplings is written $\Pi(P, Q)$.
nodes.title: Couplings

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable spaces and $c \colon X \times Y \to [0, \infty]$ a cost function. The Kantorovich cost of a measure $\pi$ on $X \times Y$ is $I(\pi) = \int_{X \times Y} c \, d\pi \in [0, \infty]$, the Lebesgue integral of $c$ against $\pi$ (for a non-measurable $c$, the lower Lebesgue integral).
nodes.title: Kantorovich cost
